subject: Export feeds and retention slicing for audit & access logs
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finvero.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Export feeds - retention slicing for EU legal hold

Hi Sofia,

Quick one from our legal team as we prep a retention/legal-hold runbook: can Redwood provide continuous export feeds for both audit logs (service/control-plane events) and access logs (tenant access traces) scoped to our EU tenant? They specifically want to know:

- Supported export formats (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV) and whether gzipping is available
- Incremental vs full snapshots (can we get hourly deltas + daily snapshot?)
- Chunking / slice granularity (size limits, time windows)
- Retention options you support on export (how long will exported slices remain accessible from your side)
- Deletion/erase semantics when we request a removal (how does that reflect in exports/manifest)
- Residency guarantees and KMS/HSM options for exported artifacts

If you can share a sample S3 manifest layout and an SLA for export delivery (and how to request extended retention for legal hold), that would be ideal.

Thanks — looping in LegalOps at Acme for context.

Best,
Laura
Director, Security Operations
Finvero
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finvero.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Export feeds - retention slicing for EU legal hold

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, followed by proposed options so you can pick what fits Finvero's legal runbook. Marissa (product) and Ben (engineering) are on CC for details and artifacts.

Summary (high-level):
- Formats: We support NDJSON and columnar Parquet for exports. NDJSON is convenient for quick search/small slices; Parquet is recommended for large-volume analytics. All exports can be gzipped for transfer efficiency.
- Snapshot cadence: We offer daily full snapshots and configurable incremental deltas (hourly or every 6 hours) for customers on Dedicated or Private. Hosted customers can request hourly deltas via an export job.
- Chunking: Default chunking target is ~200–300MB compressed per file; time-window slicing is configurable (hourly/daily). We can also slice by tenant + region to minimize cross-tenant artifacts.
- Export retention (on our delivery tier): by default exported artifacts are retained for 90 days in the export bucket. For enterprise contracts we offer extended retention (180 days / 1 year / multi-year archival) on request.
- Deletion semantics: Exported files are immutable once written; deletion requests for source logs trigger tombstone markers and a separate expunge job. For legal hold we can preserve existing exports and provide a certificate of preservation; for erasure requests we can remove future exports and produce an audit event showing removal requests and manifest updates.
- Residency & keys: Exports for EU tenants can be delivered to an EU S3 endpoint; Customer-managed KMS keys are supported for Dedicated and Private plans.

Actionable next steps I propose:
1) We prepare a short sample S3 manifest and a small NDJSON/Parquet example (will attach).
2) If you need extended retention or immutable archival, let us know target retention and whether you want us to copy exports to a customer-owned bucket (we recommend customer-owned S3 for long-term archival).
3) Ben will outline the manifest layout and the incremental feed mechanism (object prefix + manifest file) below.

I attached a residency/retention matrix and a sample manifest; Ben — can you add the technical details on the incremental feed and deletion flow?

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@finvero.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-08T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Export feeds - retention slicing for EU legal hold

Hi all — Marissa from Product. Adding technical specifics so Finvero can validate against LegalOps requirements. Ben, I left a couple of notes inline.

Format & compression:
- NDJSON: newline-delimited JSON, good for log-centric tooling and small exports.
- Parquet: columnar, recommended for analytics and large-volume restores. Supports schema evolution; we write snapshotted partitioned Parquet by date and tenant id.
- Compression: Gzip or Snappy for Parquet. We gzip NDJSON by default for transfers.

Manifest / incremental feed model (what we deliver):
- Manifest (manifest.json) includes: export_id, tenant_id, region, time_window_start, time_window_end, file_list (objects with path + size + checksum), sequence_number.
- Incremental deltas: We publish an hourly delta manifest plus the delta files. Each manifest increments sequence_number and references prior manifest id for chaining. This allows you to replay or apply deltas without missing events.
- Delivery options: 
  * Push to a Redwood-managed staging bucket (default, 90-day retention)
  * Push to a customer-provided S3 bucket (recommended for long-term/legal hold). When pushing to customer S3 we can use server-side encryption with your KMS.

Chunking & size policy:
- Target compressed chunk size: 250MB (adjustable). We avoid slicing records mid-event; chunk boundaries are on event timestamps.
- If a single hour exceeds chunk target we slice across sub-hour windows and provide multiple files with contiguous time ranges.

Deletion & legal hold:
- Once files are pushed to a customer-owned bucket, Redwood guarantees we will not delete them. If files remain in our staging bucket, we can apply retention rules and produce a signed deletion certificate when files are removed.
- For source-level erasure requests: we perform tombstoning (logical delete) and then schedule physical purge per the contract. Exports already delivered to your bucket are not auto-removed by us unless explicitly requested with signed approval.

Sample manifest layout (short):
{
  "export_id": "exp-20260807-eu-finvero-01",
  "tenant_id": "finvero-eu",
  "time_window_start": "2026-08-07T00:00:00Z",
  "time_window_end": "2026-08-07T01:00:00Z",
  "sequence_number": 10234,
  "files": [
    {"path": "eu/finvero/2026/08/07/00/logs-0001.parquet.gz", "size": 23456789, "sha256": "..."}
  ]
}

Ben (engineering) — a couple of notes on manifest format and how customers can consume incremental feeds (S3 prefix + manifest polling / SQS notify).

Marissa
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finvero.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Export feeds - retention slicing for EU legal hold

Hi Laura — Ben from Engineering. A few practical items and next steps so you can validate with LegalOps: 

1) Sample artifacts attached: audit-export-sample-manifest.json (small NDJSON + manifest) and residency-retention-matrix.pdf. The manifest uses the chained sequence_number model; we also include a small sidecar index (manifest.index.json) for fast lookups.

2) Recommended consumption pattern: use an SQS notification on the export prefix and process manifests in sequence. We include a last-processed-sequence checkpoint in the manifest metadata so consumers can verify idempotency.

3) SLA & delivery guarantees: for hosted exports we publish manifests within 30 minutes of window close for daily snapshots and within 10 minutes for hourly delta manifests (subject to load). For Dedicated/Private we offer contractual SLAs with faster SLAs and options for streaming via a private egress link.

4) Extended retention: If Finvero wants us to hold exports beyond our default 90 days on Redwood-managed storage, we can either:
   - Push copies to your customer-owned bucket (preferred) OR
   - Keep on Redwood-managed archival for N months/years under an addendum (we’ll provide immutability flags and preservation certificates).

5) Deletion flow: if a GDPR/erase request comes through for a subject that appears in historical export slices, our workflow is: 
   - Identify events by event_id and mark tombstone in search index
   - Flag the relevant export manifests and add a deletion_note entry
   - If files live in Redwood-managed bucket: schedule removal after approval and provide signed deletion record
   - If files in customer bucket: we advise you to perform removal; we can provide the list of affected objects and a verification badge

Next step: Sofia — can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk LegalOps through the sample manifest and the S3/SQS consumption pattern? Laura — if you confirm a preferred retention target (e.g., 2 years archival to customer bucket), we’ll include that in the export job template.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

On attachments: audit-export-sample-manifest.json (manifest + small file pointers), residency-retention-matrix.pdf (matrix with options & pricing tiers).
